controls.title: Maintain an executable incident response plan
controls.statement: Maintain a current incident response plan that assigns accountable roles, covers the full incident lifecycle and defines internal, external and third-party coordination.
controls.risk: During a serious incident, unclear authority and improvised coordination can delay decisions, increase disruption and produce inconsistent communication.
controls.scope: Cyber security incidents affecting business services, information, technology, suppliers and operational technology.
controls.examine: Review the response plan, role assignments, contact lists, declaration criteria, communications arrangements, playbooks and approval and review history.
controls.interview: Ask incident, technology, business, legal and communications leaders who can declare an incident and how decisions and handoffs are coordinated.
controls.test: Walk a representative scenario through the plan and confirm that current personnel can locate it, understand their authority and contact required parties.
controls.expected: The current plan is available during disruption, covers the incident lifecycle and gives named roles clear authority, actions and communication paths.

mappings.basis: Requires each entity to develop and exercise a cyber security incident management and response plan.
Requires an organisation-specific response plan defining structure, reportable incidents, resources, responsibilities and distribution.
Requires a maintained incident response process covering roles, compliance requirements and communications.
Requires designated primary and backup personnel to coordinate and document incident handling.
Requires maintained response plans covering all phases of the incident lifecycle.
Requires security incident management and response plans to be incorporated into business continuity arrangements.

controls.title: Analyse, contain and recover from incidents
controls.statement: Use a consistent incident-handling process to validate reports, establish scope and cause, contain harm, remove the cause and restore normal operations.
controls.risk: An incident that is misunderstood or contained too slowly can spread to more systems, prolong service disruption and cause avoidable loss of information.
controls.scope: Declared or suspected cyber security incidents from initial triage through containment, eradication and recovery.
controls.examine: Inspect incident records, triage decisions, analysis artefacts, timelines, containment actions, eradication evidence, recovery approvals and coordination logs.
controls.interview: Ask responders how they confirm an incident, determine its boundaries, choose containment actions and decide that recovery is safe.
controls.test: Trace sampled incidents from report through closure and verify that each handling stage, decision owner and supporting evidence is recorded.
controls.expected: Sampled incidents are validated, analysed and contained promptly, their cause is addressed and recovery is authorised with a clear decision trail.

mappings.basis: Requires preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication and recovery through a consistent handling capability.
Requires incident reports to be triaged and validated.
Requires analysis to establish what occurred and its root cause.
Correlation of event information supports incident analysis but does not establish the complete handling process.

controls.title: Exercise response and apply lessons
controls.statement: Exercise incident response using realistic scenarios, evaluate decisions and communications, and track lessons and corrective actions to completion.
controls.risk: An untested response may fail when pressure is highest, allowing known weaknesses in plans, communications and recovery decisions to persist.
controls.scope: Incident response personnel, executives, business owners, suppliers and technical teams with response responsibilities.
controls.examine: Review the exercise schedule, scenarios, participants, observations, post-incident reviews, corrective actions, owners, deadlines and plan updates.
controls.interview: Ask response leaders how scenarios are selected, executives and suppliers are involved and overdue improvements are escalated.
controls.test: Select completed exercises and real incidents and trace significant lessons through assigned corrective actions to verified closure and updated plans.
controls.expected: Exercises test realistic decisions and communication paths, and material lessons from exercises and incidents result in completed, verified improvements.

mappings.basis: Requires annual cyber security incident response testing.
Requires lessons learned and a post-incident review following significant incidents or crises.
Requires testing the effectiveness of the incident response capability.
Requires routine response exercises testing communications, decisions and workflows.
Requires post-incident reviews that identify lessons and follow-up actions.
Requires periodic and trigger-based response plan exercises.
Requires lessons-learned activities and corrective updates to the response plan.
